Q79934771.summary: This pendant is made of two dome-shaped pieces of rock crystal in a gold mount, one cut on its reverse with a tiny intaglio of the Anastasis. Christ, holding a cross-staff, reaches out to Adam, who kneels before him, while Eve stands behind, also stretching out her hand. Seen through the clear crystal, the image of Christ raising the first parents from death would have been carried close to the body as a sign of hope in the Resurrection.
facts: The Anastasis shows Christ entering the gates of Hell to release the righteous of the Old Testament, beginning with Adam and Eve.
The Cleveland Museum of Art notes that the gold chain may be of later date than the pendant.
The crystal pendant measures only 4.2 × 3.3 cm.
Q79934771.notes: Museum dates it to the late 500s (Byzantium). The intaglio is too small to read clearly in the general photograph; the description follows the museum's text.

commons:197439603.summary: A plain stone cross set against the crypt wall bears at its crossing a carved bearded head with heavy-lidded eyes, a drooping moustache and hair rendered in parallel grooves. Placed where the head of the Crucified would be, the face is generally read as Christ, reduced to a stark and solemn mask. The cross is known locally as the 'Merovingian Cross', though its origin and date are not documented in sources available to us.
facts: Descriptions of Würzburg Cathedral (e.g. an older version of the German Wikipedia article, mirrored online) caption it simply 'Merowingerkreuz in der Domkrypta'; the name implies, but does not prove, an origin in the Merovingian period (before c. 750).
commons:197439603.notes: Identification of the head as Christ and the date both rest only on the Commons category ('10th-century reliefs of Jesus Christ') and the popular name 'Merowingerkreuz' (which would imply a pre-750 date); no museum or scholarly record was found. Material inferred from the photograph. Treat as uncertain; consider removing if no source can be found.

cur:manuscripts-otto-iii-gethsemane-arre.summary: In the upper register Christ appears twice on the rocky Mount of Olives: prostrate in prayer and then standing to rouse the sleeping apostles. Below, soldiers with clubs and torches surround him as Judas kisses him, and a figure crouches at the lower right.
facts: The Gospels of Otto III has 276 leaves, twelve canon tables, a double-page portrait of the emperor, four evangelist portraits and 29 full-page miniatures of New Testament scenes; it was produced at Reichenau around 1000.
Its original cover still holds a 10th-century Byzantine ivory of the Dormition of the Virgin.
cur:manuscripts-otto-iii-gethsemane-arre.notes: Folio not given on the Commons/WGA source.
